contract.source: one admitted Program and separately sealed LoweringPlan under the same source revision
contract.ordering: one deterministic depth-first event stream in grammar source order
contract.record_payload: stable FieldId carried by EnterField and LeaveField
contract.transaction: candidate events become observable only when their enclosing parse transaction commits
contract.resource_policy: caller-selected LimitsConfig can only tighten baked input-byte, nesting, logical-event, and work ceilings; typed fault kinds are preserved in both recognition and retained-event calls
contract.kernel_abi: generated Rust asserts parse_that::KERNEL_ABI == 2 at compile time and the BBNF carrier requires parse_that =0.4.1 exactly
contract.runtime_grammar_policy: generated controls do not deserialize, interpret, or traverse a runtime grammar
contract.host_action_policy: generated controls contain no callback, closure, trait object, dynamic dispatch, or host-code execution surface

control_law.complete_packet: replay_compilation and CompiledModule::from_replay_json validate bbnf.compiled-module.v5, recompile the carried source under caller-supplied CompileOptions including analysis_work, and reject option, component, generated-byte, revision, or canonical-byte disagreement
control_law.analysis_packet: the complete packet carries bbnf.analysis-facts.v3 with required iterations and work_units; the recursive nominal-record schema probe records iterations=4 and work_units=78
control_law.generated_source: GeneratedModule::emit consumes ScalarEventPlan and LoweringPlan as separate revision-equal sealed inputs; ScalarEventPlan does not embed lowering
control_law.stage_packets: individual replay_json methods are deterministic serializers only and have no public standalone inverse
control_law.stream_comparison: every claimed equality compares the full ordered event vector, including kind, start, end, rule, node, field, transform, and kind-specific value
control_law.failure_observation: rejected parses expose no candidate event prefix

generated_scalar.oracle: a hand-authored recognizer and expected-event constructor in the generated control test; it neither calls the emitted parser nor imports compiler carriers
generated_scalar.qualification: the scalar grammar contains no records, so the independent ExpectedEvent shape omits field; no emitted event in this control can carry one

recursive.oracle: a literal ten-event vector for the admitted recursive input (x), authored independently of the emitted parser
recursive.qualification: the additional accepted/rejected corpus asserts complete results and rollback, not an independent event constructor for every input

record.oracle: a literal twenty-two-event vector for the admitted retained/discarded-field input (x), including exact FieldId placement
record.qualification: the canonical digest is a test receipt over that exact vector, not a production checksum API

coverage: both choice branches
five digit variants
one through seven repeated pairs
trailing-input and malformed-token rejection
fixed-seed accepted and rejected generated documents
transactional rollback
logical-event thresholds equal committed stream length across shallow and deep failed speculation
allocation-free NoSink recognition and EventBuffer retention
typed InputBytes, Nesting, Events, and Work limits
stable source identity and imports
productive consuming recursion

transactional rollback on recursive failure
mode-invariant typed resource faults
stable source identity and imports
retained field descriptors are static generated data
EnterField and LeaveField carry the expected FieldId
discarded slots remain recognized but emit no field boundary

no runtime grammar or host action surface

sink_modes.recognition: check and check_with_limits use allocation-free counting NoSink; event closures are not constructed, but logical event length participates in transaction checkpoints
sink_modes.retained: parse_events and parse_events_with_limits use EventBuffer over the same borrowed immutable input and retain ScalarEvent values with source-relative byte ranges
sink_modes.transfer: EventBuffer::into_stream transfers revision, borrowed source, and the exact retained Vec without changing event order
sink_modes.equality_law: NoSink committed length equals EventBuffer committed length, and the minimum successful logical-event limit equals that length even when failed branch speculation differs
sink_modes.excluded: generated controls expose no callback mode or host-action sink

transaction_laws: choice candidates publish only after the selected branch commits
repeat candidates publish only after each repetition commits
record field boundaries publish only with their enclosing record candidate
a rejected complete parse exposes no events
resource-limit rejection exposes no candidate prefix
failed alternatives restore both cursor and sink length, including allocation-free NoSink's logical count
logical-event budget measures committed stream length; speculative event work remains accounted only by the monotone work budget
no semantic callback can escape before commit because W2 executes no host callbacks

identity_laws.schema_revision: event schema revision is explicitly bbnf.scalar-events.v4
identity_laws.grammar_revision: every generated event plan is bound to the compiler Revision carried by the complete packet
identity_laws.compiler_identity: public compiler capabilities contain the exact full Revision and a private u32 local ordinal, while persistent event rows retain compact local ordinals; same-index foreign-revision lookups are rejected
identity_laws.serialization_opacity: public capabilities and sealed carriers are not serde::Serialize; private replay adapters and generated ScalarEvent fields expose only compact grammar-local u32 ordinals under revision-bearing envelopes
identity_laws.representation_ceiling: EventSiteData and TransformSiteData are each capped at 32 bytes and Option<PlanNodeIx> at 8 bytes by colocated representation laws
identity_laws.wire_version_law: the in-memory capability/local-index split did not alter the already-compact event wire shape, so ScalarEventPlan remains v4; generated-rust v5 and generated-module v4 remain stable, while analysis-facts v3 and compiled-module v5 advance the repaired analysis and aggregate contracts
identity_laws.source_identity: generated modules expose the admitted canonical source identity
identity_laws.field_identity: FieldId is assigned by the compiler and preserved through type, lowering, event planning, emission, and the generated static descriptor table
identity_laws.transform_identity: TransformId is compiler-assigned and preserved as metadata only

checksum_law.algorithm: the test's canonical event-vector serialization followed by SHA-256
checksum_law.non_claim: the runtime API does not expose an event checksum and the scalar and recursive controls do not use this digest as their primary oracle

public_nameability.meaning: all public return types have public re-exported names

limitations: The generated Rust controls are correctness controls, not a claim of a finalized totality emitter or hand-rolled assembly backend.
The independent scalar oracle is grammar-specific test code; it does not establish universal differential equivalence for every future grammar feature.
The record digest detects change in one canonical vector; it is not a collision-proof semantic proof.
W2 transforms are declarative event metadata and do not execute host code.
